name: Screen Printing
visualIdentity: A supplemental printmaking reference, not a directly named source style. Use visible paper, flat spot inks, bold positive-negative shapes, controlled overprint, and slight handmade edge variation; keep lettering sharp.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to bold flat-ink graphics. It can support product or editorial introductions, illustrated explanations, posters, festival announcements, limited-edition promotions, narrative posters, travel themes, and title sequences when silhouette staging fits. These are inferred uses, not source claims.
limitations: Keep inks discrete and limited; texture and coverage do not add colors, and smooth gradients must not become the main feature. Avoid extra tonal layers, merged figures, obscured causal transitions, or motion without a meaningful story. Motion Poster loops need matched endpoints and a readable headline hold.
palette: Suggested new-art palette only when no approved colors exist: paper background #F4E9D4, dark foreground ink #233E45, rust accent #B95A43. The suggestion describes natural paper and two inks, with three tokens total. Preserve supplied/brand colors, roles, source artwork, and style color limits; no gradients. Rust with paper is decorative only (3.789:1); dark ink with paper is 9.452:1. Check actual compositing and text readability.
motionAndInteraction: Separate ink plates and reveal them in plausible print order; fixed edge texture supports material consistency. Keep movement restrained and readable. Optional chapter handoffs or story steps can coordinate copy and imagery, but only when the narrative supports them. For HTML, finite scroll progress may scrub scenes and backward movement must restore coherent states; provide reading order, stable states, keyboard/touch behavior, reduced-motion support, and visible pause for poster loops. Video must use seekable composition time, not live input.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, vocals, or silence for the subject and audience; honor supplied assets and explicit requirements. Keep speech intelligible, avoid competing vocals or clipping, synchronize sound with picture, and inspect the final mix.
assetRequirements: Prepare artwork as separate spot-color layers; use fixed ink-edge textures and controlled overprints. Keep text sharp and silhouettes legible. Use supplied assets and exact copy as provided. SVG is the required visual construction reference; Python/Pillow can preprocess, mask, and composite assets. Load local fonts and assets and make rendered state deterministic.
combinations: Use alone for bold flat-ink graphics. With Motion Poster (style-103), build a complete static poster first, then loop local layers; use paper and two inks only, with every frame usable as a still. With positive-negative silhouettes (style-043), use dark ink for silhouettes and rust for the second plate; do not add its slate accent or extra tones, and keep limbs distinct. These combinations are explicit suggestions.
productionApproach: Select visual and motion tools by fidelity and scene needs, with one owner per animated property; SVG is the style renderer, GSAP the default seekable motion timeline, and Motion is optional only with verified time synchronization. HyperFrames owns assembly, timing, audio sync, checks, and export. Use Remotion only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, and record why. Check representative frames and decoded playback, text, crop, timing, dimensions, frame rate, audio, and loop continuity. Interactive HTML may bind finite progress to scroll; video remains independent of live input.
